extracted.intended_audience: AISTATS 2016 paper reviewers (program committee, area chairs, external reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing submissions to the AISTATS 2016 double-blind conference, including review structure, evaluation criteria for different contribution types, procedural rules (CMT/conflicts), and confidentiality/code/data policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure — overview paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Each review should begin with a paragraph providing an overview of the paper, and summarising its main contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give some thought to how the paper fits with the aims and topics of the conference (not interpreted overly narrowly). Relate the ideas presented to previous work in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure — major comments section
rubrics_metrics.description: The next section of the review should deal with major comments, issues that the reviewer sees as standing in the way of acceptance of the paper, or issues that should be addressed prior to publication, or reasons for rejecting the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly identify substantive flaws or missing elements that would prevent acceptance; articulate what must be changed or demonstrated for the paper to be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure — minor issues section
rubrics_metrics.description: The final section of the review should deal with any minor issues, such as typographical errors, spelling mistakes, or areas where presentation could be improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List small corrections and presentation suggestions separately from major scientific concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code/data request policy in initial reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: For AISTATS 2016, reviewers may request code (and as necessary, accompanying data) in the initial reviews, which will be provided as part of the author response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request code/data only if it is the deciding factor in paper acceptance. Requests should be reasonable given the duration of the discussion period. The SPC member in charge will confirm whether the request is warranted and reasonable. Authors may only submit separate code and data at the invitation of a reviewer; otherwise usual restrictions apply on author response length. The conference chairs will enable anonymous transfer of code and data to the relevant reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code/data usage and disposal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer requests code and accompanying data, this is provided for the reviewer's sole use and only for assessing the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All code and data must be discarded once the review is complete, and may not be used in further research or transferred to third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code/data anonymization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer requests code from the authors, this code should be anonymized (e.g. author names should be removed from the file headers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers understand it might be difficult to remove all traces of the authors from the files and will exercise reasonable judgment if innocent mistakes are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution categories for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions of AISTATS papers can be categorised into four areas: a) algorithmic, b) theoretical, c) unifying or d) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper may exhibit one or more of these contributions; each is important in advancing the state of the art. Reviewers should judge the paper according to these relevant contribution types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic contributions may make a particular approach feasible for the first time or may extend the applicability of an approach (for example allowing it to be applied to very large data sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scalability, practicality, and whether the algorithm enables new kinds of problems to be solved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: A theoretical contribution should provide a new result about a model or algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include convergence proofs, consistency proofs or performance guarantees; assess rigor, relevance, and novelty of theoretical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unifying contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: A unifying contribution may bring together several apparently different ideas and show how they are related, providing new insights and directions for future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity of the unification and the new insights or research directions it enables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: An application contribution should typically have aspects that present particular statistical challenges which require solution in a novel way or through clever adaptation of existing techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the statistical challenge, novelty or cleverness of the adaptation, and empirical rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage work relating machine learning and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: AISTATS is particularly keen to see work which relates machine learning and statistics or highlights novel connections between the fields or even contrasts them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give favorable consideration to papers that bridge or contrast the two fields and clarify their contributions in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report failure cases
rubrics_metrics.description: One aspect of result presentation that is often neglected is a discussion of the failure cases of an algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description of failure cases as well as successes should be encouraged and rewarded in submissions; do not penalize authors for honestly reporting failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look for thought-provoking or paradigm-shifting work
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the most important aspects of a successful conference paper is that it should be thought provoking. Thought provoking papers sometimes generate strong reactions on initial reading, which may sometimes be negative. However, if the paper genuinely represents a paradigm shift it may take a little longer than a regular paper to come around to the author's way of thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an eye out for such papers; they may take longer to review but may represent important advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and acceptance standard (journal-like expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is envisioned in exactly the same spirit as in a top quality journal like JRSS B, JASA, or Annals of Statistics. Accepted contributions are published in proceedings, and acceptance is competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AISTATS does not give the option to revise and resubmit: if a paper cannot be accepted with minor revisions (e.g. as proposed by the authors in their response to the reviews), it should be rejected. Emphasize required levels of quality and innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The AISTATS reviewing process is confidential. By agreeing to review you agree not to use ideas, results, code, and data from submitted papers in your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes research and grant proposals unless the work has appeared in other publicly available formats (e.g. technical reports, published work). Do not distribute submitted papers, ideas, code, or data to anyone else unless permission is gained from the program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind process and deanonymisation prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: AISTATS 2016 is a double blind reviewed conference. Whilst authors are expected to remove identity-revealing information, reviewers are trusted not to take positive steps to try and uncover the authors' identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may see that authors have posted tech reports (e.g. arXiv) but should not seek out such reports on line to deanonymize. Authors do not know reviewer identities; area chairs do see reviewer identities; during discussion reviewer identities will be made available to other reviewers to facilitate discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter conflicts of interests in CMT as domain names and/or by marking specific authors with whom you have a conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark a conflict with anyone who is or ever was your student or mentor, is a current or recent colleague, or is a close collaborator. If in doubt, mark the conflict to avoid appearance of impropriety. Your own username should be automatically marked, but check for duplicate accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMT system procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the CMT system to enter conflicts, provide subject keywords for allocation, submit and revise reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can revise your review multiple times before submission. The formal invite comes from CMT; the invite email is your login. You can change your password with the password reset from the login screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is allowed by AISTATS 2016 (e.g. proofs, video, source code or audio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a reviewer you should feel free to make use of this supplementary material to help in your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submission to other conference venues in the areas of machine learning and statistics is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneous submission to journal publications of significantly extended versions of the paper is permitted, as long as the publication date of the journal is not before June 2016.
